HPI: 27-year-old woman with new episodes of fast irregular fluttering centered in the chest. First episode was 2 weeks ago; current continuous episode began 6 hours ago. Earlier episodes lasted 10 minutes. Current episode began at rest while working and has not stopped with rest or avoiding coffee today. Energy drinks appear to trigger episodes. Mild exertional dyspnea, fatigue and discomfort with ordinary walking. No previous episodes before this illness.

Perspective: Does this mean I am having a heart attack?

PSH: No surgeries or hospitalizations.

Meds: Amlodipine 5 mg daily; no supplements or decongestants.

Allergies: Penicillin causes hives.

SH: Never smoked tobacco. Two beers most evenings. No cocaine, amphetamines or other recreational drugs. Software analyst; lives with husband; drinks 3 energy drinks on workdays.

FH: Mother has hypertension; father has atrial fibrillation; sister is healthy; no sudden death before age 50.

ROS: Cardiovascular - Reports palpitations. Denies chest pain. Denies syncope. Respiratory - Reports dyspnea. Denies cough. Denies hemoptysis. General - Denies fever. Reports fatigue. Denies weight loss.
Reproductive history: I do not think I am pregnant, but I have not taken a pregnancy test.
Reproductive history: My last period was 2 weeks ago.

General: Alert. Speaking comfortably at rest.
Heart: Tachycardic and irregularly irregular rhythm; no murmur heard.
Lungs: In the examined posterior fields, bilateral breath sounds without crackles or wheeze.
Heart: Radial pulse is rapid and irregular.
Neck: Thyroid not enlarged and nontender.
Osteopathic: T1 paraspinal tissue texture change with mild tenderness on the right.
Skin: No visible rash on the inspected arms.
P: 1. Obtain a 12-lead ECG now and assess hemodynamic stability; check BMP, magnesium, CBC and thyroid tests; arrange same-day emergency department evaluation for rate/rhythm and stroke-risk assessment; explain uncertainty until ECG confirmation and seek emergency help for chest pain, syncope or worsening dyspnea.

2. Review energy drinks, alcohol and sympathomimetic exposure; advise stopping energy drinks and discuss reducing alcohol; arrange symptom/rhythm follow-up rather than assuming all episodes are benign.
3. Obtain TSH with reflex thyroid hormones; examine for thyroid signs and review weight/heat intolerance; refer for targeted treatment if results support thyroid disease.

HPI: 27-year-old woman with new episodes of fast irregular fluttering centered in the chest. First episode was 2 weeks ago; current continuous episode began 6 hours ago. Earlier episodes lasted 10 minutes. Current episode began at rest while working and has not stopped with rest or avoiding coffee today. Energy drinks appear to trigger episodes. Mild exertional dyspnea, fatigue and discomfort with ordinary walking. No previous episodes before this illness.

FH: Mother has hypertension; father has atrial fibrillation; sister is healthy; no sudden death before age 50.

reasoning.question: Is it happening continuously now, and exactly when did this episode begin?
reasoning.why: The current episode duration differs from the date of the first-ever palpitation.
reasoning.if_present: Persistent symptoms make ECG capture and stability assessment immediately useful.
reasoning.if_absent: Intermittent resolved symptoms may require rhythm monitoring rather than a reassuring single normal pulse.
reasoning.next_action: Ask about syncope/chest symptoms, capture rhythm and review stimulants.
